title: R_4(5(x-y)=1z) = 625
statement: The 4-colour Rado number of 5(x-y) = 1z is exactly 625 = 5^4: every 4-colouring of {1,...,625} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 4-colouring of {1,...,624} avoids one. This replicates the published value (Chang-De Loera-Wesley, ISSAC 2022, Table 10) inside axeyum with no external solver or checker.

provenance.conjectured_by: construction + literature: Chang-De Loera-Wesley Lemma 4.1 gives R_k >= a^k for gcd(a,b)=1 by the a-adic valuation colouring, and their Theorem 1.2(3) gives equality at k=3 for a >= b+2; the k=4 value was predicted by extending that pattern

NO external solver was used anywhere in this claim (ADR-0002)

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022 / arXiv:2210.03262
prior_art.establishes: REPLICATION. Table 10 of arXiv:2210.03262 gives R_4(5(x-y)=1z) = 625; this claim reproduces it end to end with axeyum's own proof-producing CDCL and backward DRAT checker. Read from the rendered v1 PDF, whose compiled form contains Tables 9-15.

evidence.supports: identifies F_625, the formula the refutation is about
evidence.notes: 2500 variables, 287248 clauses. Re-checked by regeneration from (a,b,k,n)=(5,1,4,625) with the encoder written independently of the generator of record, not by hash alone.

NOT SEARCHED FOR. This is Chang-De Loera-Wesley's Lemma 4.1 colouring written down from the construction: point j takes colour v_5(j) + 1, the 5-adic valuation, which on [624] takes exactly the 4 values 0..3. Emitted and checked in under 0.02 s by `cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- valuation 5 1 4 624 witness.txt`. Verified four independent ways: the encoder's own first_monochromatic, the family's brute-force first_violation, CnfFormula::evaluate on the one-hot assignment, and this ledger's own Python enumerator.

regeneration.command: cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- solve 5 1 4 625 F_625.drat witness-625.txt 10
regeneration.note: The certificate is 1873245421 bytes of text DRAT and is NOT distributed: it regenerates in 1044 s from four integers, and checking it costs more than producing it. Measured on this instance, parsing plus backward-checking it needed 12.3 GiB resident for 1.87 GB on disk, so a verifier should budget roughly 7x the file size in RAM.

evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- solve 5 1 4 625 F_625.drat witness-625.txt 10
evidence.notes: Produced and checked entirely inside axeyum: the proof was streamed to disk, read back through axeyum's own parse_drat (the round trip finding B8 showed the shipped binary-DRAT certificates could not survive), and re-derived by check_drat_backward. 24184646 steps, solve 1044.164 s, check 1368.072 s. The artifact itself is not stored; the row is hash-pinned and regenerable, which is why check-claim-certificates.py reports it as NOT re-checked in this tree rather than pretending otherwise.

notes: Both sides of the threshold, each by a different mechanism: the lower bound is a construction written down and checked, the upper bound is a machine proof re-derived by an independent checker. Neither side used an external solver.
